findings.title: Public value records retain writable fields outside the earlier invariant-bearing-field fix
findings.evidence: The production lexical inventory finds 101 public fields in these seven files, excluding the private native FFI representation. The bounded witness prints representative result fields. Source declarations and callers were inspected; the inventory count is not 101 independent defects.
findings.reproduction: Run node docs/audits/AUD-025-harnesses/core-review.mjs --check (exit 1), or inspect the listed pub struct fields. A consumer can write Repaired.container_words, Argon2Cost.memory_kib, Completion.letters and WishOdds.random_bits directly.
findings.expected: CORE-02 says owner types keep fields private; CORE-11 makes fields private by default. The current guide has no general public-DTO exemption.
findings.observed: The earlier fix encapsulated NewContainer, CheckEvidence and Found, while ordinary value/result/vector records still expose fields. That earlier bounded fix is present; these additional records are a broader conformance gap.
findings.impact: Bounded maintainability and API evolution cost. Result representations are writable rather than owned behind an interface. No invalid encryption result, secret disclosure or broken invariant is demonstrated. Public vector records intentionally contain only public test data.
findings.recommendedFix: Make value/result fields private, expose the meaningful read operations and only necessary constructors, and update existing callers. Preserve serialized JSON and secret-owner lifetimes. Avoid empty wrappers introduced solely to satisfy syntax.
findings.requiredVerification: Compile native and WASM consumers; run nearest result, repair, parameter, hint, wish and serialization tests plus fast gates. Check published vector bytes or retained-round fixtures without a full-cost replay. Review public Rust API documentation and browser binding parity.

findings.title: The internal Argon2 startup error has an error-code prefix but no readonly code property
findings.evidence: A VM evaluates only the actual standalone Argon2StartError definition with synthetic build/issue values. It returns name=Argon2StartError, hasCode=false, and a message beginning INTERNAL_ERROR. No worker or Argon2 operation starts.
findings.reproduction: Run the retained harness --self-test (exit 0), then --check (exit 1). The latter prints actualStartupError.hasCode=false.
findings.expected: TS-06 requires every error class to carry a readonly code from the module code list; CORE-23 requires stable codes separate from person-facing text.
findings.observed: The class keeps typed private build/issue context and formats INTERNAL_ERROR into message, but provides no code property.
findings.impact: Limited internal error-contract inconsistency. Existing worker serialization still produces coded public failures; this probe does not establish a public API failure or a privacy regression. The sanitized context/fallback behavior is intentional and must be preserved.
findings.recommendedFix: Add a readonly code using the existing error-code source and derive the message consistently while retaining sanitized build/issue detail.
findings.requiredVerification: Run the witness and error-contract controls, JS type/lint checks, and nearest worker-startup privacy/fallback tests. Preserve rejection of arbitrary backend exception text.

findings.title: An outside EFF word index can overflow the public weighted check-word calculation
findings.evidence: The retained check-index-red test panics on usize::MAX in the fifth index; the same boundary now returns ReviewError::InvalidIndex/INVALID_REQUEST before arithmetic. All 15 nearest check-word tests pass, including literal boundary answers and startup refusal.
findings.reproduction: cargo test --locked --lib an_outside_list_index_is_refused_without_overflow; red exit 101, final exit 0.
findings.expected: Every index outside the 7,776-word list is refused without overflow, wraparound or echoing input.
findings.observed: The inherited index-level calculation multiplied unchecked usize indexes. The owner API now validates every index before the shared weighted helper.
findings.impact: Bounded input-refusal defect: invalid direct index callers could panic in a checked build or get a wrapped answer. No valid password/output mismatch or secret disclosure was demonstrated.
findings.recommendedFix: Validate all indexes at the public owner boundary and preserve valid outputs and generator error classification.
findings.requiredVerification: Literal zero/mixed/upper-bound answers, 7776 and usize::MAX refusals, generator/check-word tests and startup refusal.

findings.title: Worker round progress accepts negative, fractional and over-total counters
findings.evidence: The retained protocol-regression-red fails for the actual source with its former numeric-only guard; protocol-regression-green passes. Package checks also refuse malformed messages before invoking callbacks and terminate their workers.
findings.reproduction: node scripts/verify-browser-source.mjs; the retained former-guard control exits 1, final source exits 0.
findings.expected: Round stages carry safe integers 1 through the declared total; search candidate 0 remains a valid initial observation.
findings.observed: Finite numeric round values previously passed irrespective of sign, fraction or relation to the total. The non-search guard now enforces all three bounds.
findings.impact: Malformed worker progress could reach a page handler. No cryptographic output change or cross-worker code execution is demonstrated.
findings.recommendedFix: Validate safe-integer rounds and bounds before callback dispatch while preserving valid search/progress messages.
findings.requiredVerification: Negative/fractional/zero/over-total refusals, each valid stage/total and endpoints, initial search 0 and package protocol/cancellation checks.

findings.title: An overlong BIP39 token is copied before its inevitable refusal
findings.evidence: Static review confirmed typed_word called to_ascii_lowercase before any token-length guard. Public Phrase::read tests now refuse a 9-byte and a 100,000-byte synthetic token with the same position/code and no input echo. Both real-browser smokes also refuse an overlong token.
findings.reproduction: cargo test --locked --lib an_overlong_word_is_refused_at_its_position_without_echoing_it; exit 0 after the guard.
findings.expected: An impossible English word or prefix is refused before an unnecessary secret allocation.
findings.observed: The shared reader now checks LONGEST_WORD before lowercasing. Every accepted English word and prefix remains within this bound.
findings.impact: Unnecessary input-proportional transient allocation on malformed input; no external exploit, global allocator bound or actual secret-memory residue is claimed.
findings.recommendedFix: Apply the existing longest-word bound before allocating the lowercase copy.
findings.requiredVerification: Public boundary refusals, normalization/prefix known answers, native/WASM checks and real-worker overlong refusal.

limitations: This is a solo scoped CORE conformance assessment, not a new full security/all-files audit or independent completeness review.
All 336 first-party code files were inventoried; manual inspection focused on relevant interfaces, copied facts and prior findings. Inventory is not line-by-line review of all 336 files.

The Rust lexical reader excludes test-only items, but is not a semantic Rust parser and may miss macros or alternate declaration forms. Public field/function counts are candidates, not separate finding totals.
No full-cost Argon2, full vector replay, canonical Docker build, fresh browser matrix or Windows/macOS native acceptance was executed.
The earlier AUD-024 154 verified / 4 fixed / 1 accepted disposition is historical and scoped; it does not establish literal compliance with every CORE review rule.
No production, test, dependency, workflow, vector, specification, browser package or neighboring repository was changed during this baseline.

The 4-8 hour implementation estimate is an engineering range, with up to 12 hours contingency for public API/caller migration. Platform/canonical acceptance is separate and cannot be scheduled without the required hosts/artifacts.
